assignment_description:
⍞ Materials: Cultural Backgrounds Study Bible, Introducing the New Testament, Luke for Everyone, notebook

➜ INTRO
Each year in HS, we will be reading one of the Gospels along with our study of the rest of the New Testament books. This year, we will be reading Luke along with Galatians, Philippians, and Colossians. It is helpful to be continually reminded of who Jesus is and how he interacted with people. The Gospel accounts were designed to be read many times. There will be insights gained that you would only pick up after multiple readings and by paying attention to repeated words and themes.

We will make use of the Cultural Backgrounds Study Bible notes and maps, Introducing the New Testament (selections), a Luke commentary (selections), and some Bible Project videos to help us understand what Luke and Paul are saying to their audiences. Then we can think about what new thoughts about God we gain in the process. You do not need to read all the study notes for all the verses. Pick and choose based on which verses you have questions about. Use a digital or physical notebook to record your thoughts as you work your way through the readings.

➜ VIEW & NARRATE
Today and over the next few weeks, we will set the stage for reading Luke and the Epistles by gaining some context. Narrate silently in your head or by talking to yourself to go over the main points. Write down a few of them in your journal.
∞ Video Link: How to Read the New Testament

➜ READ & NARRATE
Introducing the New Testament
Ch.1 p.17-24
Make a list with a short description of the rulers in Palestine at the time of Jesus.

➜ MAP WORK
When places are named in the text, refer to a map in the Study Bible or in the Introducing the NT book. Finding the places on the map is very helpful for seeing the stories in the context of the land. Sketching your own maps of journeys or regions can be helpful too.

★ STUDENT/TEACHER NOTE
Instead of reading Luke for some of the lessons, consider watching and listening to Luke via the LUMO Project, which only uses the actual text of Luke but has people acting while it is read. There are many versions and many languages available. You might consider this resource for your modern language studies, too. However, be sure to ask yourself, "What did the film add visually that the Gospel text itself did not explicitly say?” as any visualization project requires interpretive decisions to be made.

assignment_teachersNote:

· Luke: Choose two and write a few paragraphs on each:
a) Tell the story of the foretelling and birth of John the Baptist.
b) Tell a few of the stories you read about when Jesus heals someone.
c) Give an account of one of the parables of Jesus.
d) Tell the story of one of the miracles of Jesus.
Then, write a paragraph telling about what was most significant to you in Luke.
